tasks.short: Evaluate event results and agree improvements for future events.

steps.what: Send the post-event survey to attendees through the {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}.
Gather survey responses, attendance, costs and delivery notes into an evaluation workbook.
Calculate event results against targets and previous comparable events.
Read comments and write an evaluation with possible improvements.

loop.input: De-identified comments, delivery notes and calculated scorecard.
loop.output: Evaluation draft with themes, supporting references and proposed improvements.
loop.check: Validate every number against the scorecard; planner checks themes, minority concerns and source references.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per event; unresolved claims return to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calculations are deterministic, but comments describe problems in varied language and need synthesis.

steps.what: Discuss causes, conflicting feedback and feasible improvements with the organising committee.
Approve improvements that change the next event's scope or budget.
Record approved improvements, owners and deadlines in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: Configure survey timing in the {MARKETING_AUTOMATION} and combine attendance, costs and responses on the {DATA_PLATFORM} for a {BI} scorecard. A bounded loop drafts a source-linked evaluation in the {DOCS}; people discuss causes and approve changes before the {WORKFLOW} creates tasks in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Event identifiers, cost timing and survey formats differ across systems. Free-text feedback also needs interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing survey configuration and connectors handle much of the flow. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building mappings and templates; bounded drafting helps with comments.
tasks.still_hard: Low response rates, non-response bias and late invoices weaken conclusions. A theme does not establish a cause.
tasks.human_edge: The planner understands which complaints reveal a real access problem, which reflect conflicting preferences and which changes are feasible.

ambition.what: Weekly improvement decisions during recurring event series.

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time assembling evaluations and more time testing changes across events. Budget and scope approval rights remain with the sponsor.

reach.task: Assess survey bias and compare results across event formats.
reach.learn: Question design, response denominators and uncertainty in small samples.

evidence.claim: Configured surveys, deterministic scorecards and source-linked drafts can reduce evaluation preparation; event-specific gains are unverified.
The digest documents a government report refund after fabricated sources appeared in AI-assisted work, supporting source checks.

assumptions: The company runs recurring events with comparable objectives.
Survey invitations use an approved audience, template and schedule.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
EU GDPR applies to attendee data; use a lawful basis, limited access and defined retention.
Access estimates include checking national consultation requirements if identifiable employee feedback is processed.
unknowns: Whether attendance, responses and costs share an event identifier.
Survey response rates and availability of comparable past results.
Whether responses contain health information or identifiable employee criticism.
Required access approvals and any applicable national consultation process.
research_questions: Which indicators predict a useful improvement rather than merely a higher satisfaction score?
Can source references and minority concerns survive summarisation reliably?
new_work: Review themes and check unsupported explanations.
Resolve missing event identifiers and late cost updates.
Maintain survey templates, metric definitions and retention settings.
Track whether approved improvements changed later results.

tasks.short: Coordinate event finances, promotional distribution and attendee inquiries.

steps.what: Review event deadlines, invoices, promotional requests and incoming inquiries.

loop.input: New messages, attachments and event references.
loop.output: Administrative worklist with event, request type, owner and proposed priority.
loop.check: Validate event identifiers and required fields; planner reviews ambiguous or urgent items.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one repair pass per item; ambiguity goes to an unassigned queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules route structured requests, but mixed free-text messages need interpretation.

steps.what: Check supplier invoices against orders, delivery evidence and the event budget.
Approve invoice exceptions and confirm budget authority for payment processing.
Reconcile actual and committed costs in the event budget workbook.
Prepare promotional materials, audience selections and distribution dates for review.
Approve promotional content, recipients and timing.
Distribute approved promotional materials through the {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}.
Read attendee inquiries and prepare answers from event information.

loop.input: Attendee inquiry and current approved event information.
loop.output: Reply draft with internal source references and missing-information flags.
loop.check: Check dates, locations and policy statements against approved records; planner reviews before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; missing facts or sensitive requests return to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed templates cover common questions; varied wording and combined questions need bounded drafting.

steps.what: Resolve sensitive requests, confirm commitments and send attendee replies.
Compile administrative status and chase overdue owners.

tasks.design: Use the {PROJECT} as the event worklist, configure invoice checks in the {ERP} and connect commitments from the {PROCUREMENT} to a budget view in the {BI}. Configure approved promotional distribution in the {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}, and use bounded loops for message routing and inquiry drafts grounded in the {DOCS}. Financial exceptions, promotional release and attendee commitments retain specific human approvals.
tasks.previous_blocker: The planner bridges financial records, campaign tools and a shared mailbox. Event references and ownership are often inconsistent.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approval, campaign and routing features cover standard actions. AI-assisted coding makes the remaining connectors cheaper; small loops handle unstructured messages.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed deliveries, accessibility requests and last-minute promises require negotiation. Reliable committed-cost data and current event information remain necessary.
tasks.human_edge: The planner resolves competing deadlines and service needs while protecting supplier and attendee relationships.

ambition.what: A reusable event administration service for occasional internal organisers.

tasks.altitude: The planner works from an exception queue and spends more time helping internal organisers handle difficult cases. Financial and promotional approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Coordinate event campaign execution and audience selection.
reach.learn: Segmentation, communication permissions and campaign release checks.

evidence.claim: Configured approvals, scheduled distribution and deterministic reconciliation suit structured event administration; inquiry drafting needs source checks.

assumptions: The planner coordinates invoice handling; the finance team executes payments through its existing controls.
Promotional assets are approved before batch preparation.
The {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT} expose usable records or exports.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
EU GDPR applies to attendee and contact data; health-related requests need restricted handling.
Consultation is assessed under national rules if queue reporting enables employee monitoring.
unknowns: Existing invoice matching, tolerances and approval configuration.
Which channels distribute promotional materials, including any physical fulfilment.
Mailbox volume, inquiry types and the quality of approved event information.
Access rights, integration availability and applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: How much routing can forms and deterministic rules handle before a model is needed?
Which inquiry types most often introduce new commitments or sensitive data?
new_work: Review ambiguous routing and inquiry drafts.
Resolve unmatched invoices and stale commitments.
Maintain event information, audience permissions and routing rules.
Monitor duplicate sends, failed integrations and overdue exceptions.

tasks.short: Agree event scope, format, budgets and progress with sponsors and organising committees.

steps.what: Arrange the sponsor or committee meeting and request outstanding inputs.
Update budget scenarios from costs, commitments and proposed scope changes.
Prepare the agenda, progress summary and decisions needed.

loop.input: Current event plan, calculated scenarios, delivery notes and open decisions.
loop.output: Briefing draft distinguishing recorded facts, proposals and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate costs against scenarios and link status claims to records; planner reviews emphasis.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per meeting; unsupported statements are omitted and flagged.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply structure, but varied notes need synthesis into a short decision agenda.

steps.what: Discuss objectives, scope, format, progress and trade-offs with sponsors and committee members.
Approve event scope, budget changes and unresolved policy exceptions.
Write the decision record and action list from meeting notes.

loop.input: Planner-written meeting notes and explicitly approved event decisions.
loop.output: Decision record draft with actions, named roles, dates and unresolved points.
loop.check: Planner verifies approval status, owners and deadlines; never infer agreement from discussion.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; uncertain decisions remain unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Meeting notes vary in wording and often mix proposals with final decisions.

steps.what: Confirm the record, update event tasks and circulate agreed actions.

tasks.design: Connect costs and commitments from the {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT} to deterministic budget scenarios, while the {CALENDAR} handles recurring meetings and input reminders. Bounded loops draft briefings and decision records in the {DOCS} from approved records and written notes. After sponsor decisions and planner confirmation, the {WORKFLOW} updates the {PROJECT} and circulates actions through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Budget preparation and meeting follow-up cross several systems. Notes often mix tentative preferences with approved commitments.
tasks.enabler_now: Scenario calculations, scheduling and action publication already suit ordinary software. Faster connector development and bounded note extraction reduce preparation work.
tasks.still_hard: Sponsors may disagree about success, acceptable cost and reputational risk. Software cannot supply authority or create agreement.
tasks.human_edge: The planner makes trade-offs understandable, notices hesitation and secures explicit commitments from people with different priorities.

ambition.what: Budget reforecast decisions at each material scope change.

tasks.altitude: The planner brings costed alternatives to discussions and spends less time preparing packs and chasing actions. Sponsor approval rights and the planner's spending authority do not change.

reach.task: Compare event investments against campaign objectives.
reach.learn: Scenario assumptions, commercial objectives and separating committed costs from forecasts.

evidence.claim: Deterministic scenarios and bounded briefing drafts can support sponsor meetings while agreement and approval remain human work.

assumptions: Committee membership, meeting cadence and reminder rules are established.
The planner records written notes; automatic recording is outside scope.
Scenario assumptions remain visible and are reviewed before use.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
EU GDPR applies to participant records; consultation under national rules is assessed if monitoring is introduced.
unknowns: Sponsor approval thresholds and the planner's delegated authority.
Availability and timeliness of committed-cost data.
Whether sponsors can access the proposed shared records.
Required access approvals and any applicable national consultation.
research_questions: Which scenario inputs most often change the sponsor's decision?
Can note extraction distinguish proposals from decisions without relying on recorded meetings?
new_work: Check scenario assumptions and stale commitments.
Review briefings and confirm decision records.
Resolve missing owners, dates and ambiguous approvals.
Maintain approval thresholds, access and integration mappings.

tasks.short: Learn event management standards and trends through publications, seminars and professional peers.

steps.what: Review publication alerts and seminar invitations to choose relevant material.
Read trade publications and record useful standards, practices and questions.

loop.input: Permitted publication text, learning priorities and source metadata.
loop.output: Reading brief with source passages, claimed changes and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Planner checks original passages, dates and jurisdiction; distinguish standards from opinion and promotion.
loop.stop: One brief and one repair pass per publication; inaccessible or unsupported material returns to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword filters find topics but cannot explain varied arguments or distinguish recommendations from requirements.

steps.what: Attend seminars, observe demonstrations and ask practical questions.
Consult meeting professionals about practical experience and emerging problems.
Choose relevant practices to test and record their rationale.

tasks.design: Configure publication alerts and a personal reading queue using the {EMAIL}, {CALENDAR} and {DOCS}. A bounded reading loop produces source-linked briefs from permitted material; the planner reads important originals, attends seminars and consults peers. Learning notes and trial proposals use shared templates in the {DOCS} and link to the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Publications arrive in different formats, and their relevance depends on the planner's events. Much of the value comes from live discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing filters and saved views organise incoming material. Source-linked reading briefs are now practical without building an autonomous research agent.
tasks.still_hard: Paywalls, reuse permissions, outdated standards and promotional claims limit coverage. Tacit knowledge and professional trust take time to develop.
tasks.human_edge: The planner asks follow-up questions, recognises context and judges whether another organiser's experience transfers to their events.

ambition.what: A quarterly event-practice clinic for occasional internal organisers.

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time sorting alerts and more time discussing and testing useful practices. Learning becomes easier to share; decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Assess practical options for reducing event impacts.
reach.learn: Evidence quality, measurement boundaries and the limits of supplier claims.

evidence.claim: Filters and source-linked reading briefs can support professional learning; seminars and peer consultation retain substantial human value.

assumptions: Publications are provided through permitted subscriptions, uploads or accessible feeds.
The tool supports voluntary learning without scoring employee performance.
Practice trial proposals follow existing budget and scope approval processes before implementation.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
EU GDPR applies to stored personal notes and contact details; national consultation rules are checked if employee tracking is added.
unknowns: Available subscriptions and permissions for automated processing.
Preferred learning topics, languages and seminar formats.
Whether internal organisers want a practice clinic.
Required account access and any applicable national consultation.
research_questions: Which source types yield actionable practices rather than repeated promotional claims?
Does a brief help the planner select useful originals without missing important qualifications?
new_work: Maintain source lists and learning priorities.
Check source passages, publication dates and jurisdiction.
Remove inaccessible material and unsupported claims.
Prepare shared learning notes and review practice trials.

role.altitude: The planner spends less time moving records, preparing packs and compiling results. Their week centres more on sponsor trade-offs, service exceptions and practical improvements; formal approval rights remain unchanged.
reach: Market research analyst: design better feedback and interpret uncertain results.
Marketing manager: connect event decisions to campaign objectives and audiences.
Sustainability specialist: assess event changes using credible evidence.
skills_to_grow: Source checking and bounded model-output review.
Facilitation, negotiation and accessible event design.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a reusable event support service for occasional organisers, combining reliable administration, costed choices and evidence-backed practice clinics. Extend decision authority only through explicit delegation.
